title: Choir and Hymn
premise: Isandro Marchetti, a property surveyor who has spent her life keeping herself unremarkable, is sent to appraise the Verrone house, a building whose rooms shift and whose doors refuse to stay counted. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, she learns she is the last descendant of the founders who bound something beneath the house—and that their ritual was left unfinished on purpose. As the house begins appraising her in return, measuring her memories and offering back the people she has lost, Isandro must choose between the invisible life she built and the inheritance she never wanted. She completes the founders' work not by sealing the door again but by taking the founders' place herself, trading her name into the house so the thing below stays fed and the town above stays safe.
about_author: Petra Blackwood is the pen name of a former architectural conservator who spent a decade documenting buildings slated for demolition. Her fiction explores what structures remember after we stop living in them.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Arriving at the Verrone house for a routine appraisal, Isandro counts eleven doors where the blueprints show ten and keeps her lights burning through the night. The emotional beat is wary competence: she has survived by being unmemorable, and the house is already memorizing her.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The eleventh door migrates between rooms; her measurements contradict themselves each morning. A neighbor, Odile, warns her that the Verrones always hired 'counters.' The beat is creeping dread as Isandro realizes the house responds to attention—hers especially.

chapters.title: What the Crew Unearthed
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Excavation for the new foundation uncovers a stone door, scratched and sealed from the inside, with the Marchetti name carved above it. That night the house shows her a memory of her grandmother humming a hymn she's never heard aloud. Beat: inheritance arrives whether invited or not.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, with Odile's recounted history. Odile reveals generations of 'counters' who kept the ritual going: names entered, hymns sung, doors tallied nightly. Every counter was a Marchetti who tried to refuse and failed. Beat: Isandro understands her invisibility was inherited armor, now failing.

chapters.title: The Hymn in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The house begins singing the hymn through the plumbing and floorboards, and each verse returns a piece of Isandro's past—a dead brother's voice, her mother's lullaby—offering love in exchange for duty. Beat: temptation; the house knows exactly what she grieves.

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. She descends to the unearthed door and finds scratch marks matching her own handwriting, though she's never been here. The founders didn't imprison something below—they imprisoned someone, and the seal is thinning because no one has taken up the count. Beat: horror of complicity across generations.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The house turns the surveyor's tools on her: rooms rearrange to display her life like a property listing—her loneliness itemized, her losses valued. It offers a trade: stay, be loved, be remembered, and let the seal break. Beat: the lowest point; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Counting Backward
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. With Odile's help she reconstructs the full ritual from the founders' ledger: the counters weren't wardens but food—each one fed memories to the thing below to keep it dreaming. The final verse requires a willing heir. Beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the threshold she sings the hymn complete, giving the house every memory it offered back—her brother, her mother, her own name—as the crew's machinery falls silent around her. Beat: climax; she chooses duty shaped by love, entering the count willingly rather than being taken.

chapters.title: Twelve Doors
chapters.summary: POV Odile, months later. The house stands quiet, sold, its doors a stable twelve. A new surveyor finds the appraisal flawless and forgets the address by evening; only Odile leaves flowers at the threshold and hums a hymn she can't place. Beat: bittersweet resolution—Isandro is gone, remembered by almost no one, which is how she'd have wanted it.
